Hi Samir / Natalie,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get HaloHealth into the Redwood production lane. To make sure the CS <-> Eng handoff is tight, I wanted to kick off a single-thread plan for access controls we need to land during onboarding (SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning, IP allowlist, and service accounts / delegation).

High-level ask: please confirm the security contacts and share the current IP ranges for your outbound egress and any static jump hosts. We’ll use the attached allowlist template to capture CIDR ranges. Also please confirm whether HaloHealth will manage SCIM provisioning from Okta (recommended) or prefer just SAML first with manual SCIM later.

Proposed mutual action items (quick):
- HaloHealth: provide primary security contact, CIDR ranges (using attached CSV), and SCIM configuration owner (if using automated provisioning) — due Wed 6/27 EOD.
- Redwood: produce service account matrix and least-privilege recommendations, validate SAML metadata, and stage IP allowlist changes in staging environment — due Fri 6/29.
- Joint: schedule a 30-min engineering handoff on Thu 6/28 to walk the SA matrix and rollback plan.

Attachments: Halo_Network_Allowlist_Template.csv (please fill), Halo_SA_matrix.xlsx (draft).

If that timeline looks tight for you, call it out and we’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll schedule the handoff invite for Thu 6/28 10:00 PT.

Thanks,

--

Hi team — attaching the SA matrix (Halo_SA_matrix.xlsx) and summarizing the recommendation here so the handoff is efficient:

- We propose three SA classes:
  * ingest-reader (least privilege) — token scope: read-only for embedding ingestion endpoints; TTL 1 hour; recommended for CI systems.
  * inference-worker — token scope: generate + streaming; TTL 4 hours; limited to specified project IDs and IP ranges.
  * admin-ops — token scope: full manage for a small ops group; TTL 30 minutes; requires 2-person approval in Prod.

RBAC notes: map Okta groups to Redwood project roles (we’ll provide mapping snippet). For auditability, each token issuance is recorded with user id, originating IP, and TTL; logs retained for 90 days by default (we can extend with our compliance add-on).

On IP allowlist approvals: proposed flow in runbook is - CS tickets request -> Security (Halo) does 1-hour review -> Redwood NetOps changes staging -> Halo confirms staging smoke -> Redwood promotes to prod. We can shorten the Halo security review if you supply a standing approver (name + email).

I’ll be on the call Thu to walk the matrix.

Best,
Ben
